label: Likelihood justification
before: An incident plan and exercises exist, but incident tracking and lessons-learned controls are at risk, so execution gaps during unfamiliar events are plausible.
after: The incident response plan, incident tracking, lessons-learned reviews, and tabletop exercises (IR-01 through IR-04) are healthy in Secureframe. Execution gaps during novel or multi-vendor incidents remain plausible.

label: Likelihood justification
before: Personnel and contractor changes recur and termination controls are at risk, making cross-team process omissions plausible.
after: Personnel and contractor changes recur. The access control policy, least-privilege provisioning, termination revocation, and access review controls (AC-04, AC-07, AC-08, AC-09) are healthy in Secureframe, but cross-team onboarding and offboarding steps can still be missed.

label: Likelihood justification
before: Access spans cloud, production, source control, and SaaS systems; AC-06 and AC-07 are at risk, making excessive or stale privilege likely without stronger lifecycle enforcement.
after: Access spans cloud, production, source control, and SaaS systems. Administrative and least-privilege access controls (AC-06, AC-07) are healthy in Secureframe, but stale or excessive privilege can accumulate between access reviews.

label: Likelihood justification
before: Access changes continuously and provisioning controls are at risk, so incomplete review coverage is plausible despite a healthy scheduled-review control.
after: Access changes continuously. Least-privilege provisioning, termination revocation, and scheduled access review controls (AC-07, AC-08, AC-09) are healthy in Secureframe, but reviews of SaaS and data systems can still miss accounts.

label: Treatment notes
before: Implement strict access controls and automated deployment processes to ensure that changes are properly tested and approved before being deployed to the production environment.
after: Development, staging, and production run in separate environments. Secureframe test NET-17 (Segregated production and development environments) validates this segregation and is passing (last passed 2026-07-20). Mapped controls CM-03, CM-04, CM-05, and AC-06 are healthy; administrative access to production is restricted by least privilege. Evidence: https://app.secureframe.com/tests/3e9e58c8-21c8-41d8-9046-0b3626c01f8c/evidence

label: Likelihood justification
before: Core network monitoring controls are unhealthy and Planera lacks a demonstrated 24/7 response function, making delayed detection likely.
after: Network monitoring and incident controls (NET-02, NET-04, NET-05, IR-01, IR-02) are healthy in Secureframe, and alerts page on-call responders through PagerDuty. Missed or delayed detection remains possible from alert coverage gaps or tuning.

label: Treatment notes
before: Define monitored sources and use cases, severity and paging rules, on-call ownership, daily alert review, response SLAs, tuning, escalation, and coverage metrics.
after: Alerts are routed through PagerDuty to on-call responders. Maintain monitored sources and use cases, severity and paging rules, on-call ownership, response expectations, tuning, and escalation.

label: Treatment notes
before: Sign up for at least one reputable security bulletin and publish to a public Slack channel.  Review each notice and create tracking issues for any that are applicable.
after: A security bulletin feed is subscribed to and published to a Slack channel. Notices are reviewed and applicable ones are tracked as issues.

label: Treatment notes
before: Schedule quarterly incident drills.  Twice a year they should be mandatory and twice they should be cancel-able.  Cancellation is acceptable if there have been incidents of note during the current quarter or there are delivery pressures.
after: Incident drills are held quarterly. Two per year are mandatory; the other two may be cancelled when there have been notable incidents that quarter or there are delivery pressures.

label: Likelihood justification
before: The active red-team report documents material security findings and rapid AI development expands the attack surface, making security omission likely despite general change controls.
after: Findings from the red-team assessment have been remediated. Rapid AI development continues to expand the attack surface, so security omissions remain possible despite change controls.

label: Likelihood justification
before: Secrets and sensitive context cross repositories, CI, cloud, support, and AI execution; red-team evidence identifies credential-handling concerns, making leakage plausible.
after: Secrets and sensitive context cross repositories, CI, cloud, support, and AI execution. Credential-handling findings from the red-team assessment have been remediated; leakage remains plausible given the number of systems involved.

label: Likelihood justification
before: Repository red-team evidence documents critical and high AI-path findings, so accepting unchanged residual risk is not defensible until production applicability and remediation are verified.
after: Critical and high findings in AI code paths from the red-team assessment have been remediated. AI design, deployment, tool authorization, and operation remain complex and change frequently.

label: Treatment notes
before: Replace acceptance with mitigation: govern lifecycle stages, threat-model AI paths, verify identity and tenant boundaries, gate tools by capability, secure secrets, red-team releases, monitor abuse, and verify decommissioning.
after: Govern lifecycle stages, threat-model AI paths, verify identity and tenant boundaries, gate tools by capability, secure secrets, red-team releases, monitor abuse, and verify decommissioning.
